creative.body:
💔 I ruined a pair of khakis at 10:15am on a Saturday because of a Miralax cleanout.

Fifteen minutes into my granddaughter's soccer game I honestly thought something ruptured inside me.

Not because I took too much.

I followed the instructions my doctor gave me exactly.

😣 It started fine enough.

Mixed the whole bottle into Gatorade like the internet said. Drank it over two hours Friday night.

Within a few hours, things were moving.

I was so relieved. Finally. After eleven days of nothing, finally something was happening.

Then 2am hit.

The cramping came like a switch flipped.

I am not exaggerating when I say I grabbed the bathroom counter and held on.

Waves. One after another. The kind that make you sweat through your shirt.

I thought about waking my husband up. Thought about the ER.

But I knew what I'd taken. So I waited.

💔 By 3am I was back and forth from bed to toilet every twenty minutes.

Shaking. Sweating. Not sleeping. Counting the minutes.

8am. The cramping slowed down enough to stand.

9:45am. Drove to the soccer field thinking the worst was over.

10:15am. A feeling.

Not enough warning.

Not enough time.

😭 The khakis didn't survive.

My dignity didn't either.

I sat in my car in the parking lot with a blanket over my lap while my husband told Lily I wasn't feeling well.

And my gut?

Still hadn't actually fixed itself.

Two days later — same constipation. Same bloating. Same silence.

The cleanout had given me the worst night of my year and changed absolutely nothing.

I sat in that car thinking one thing:

There has to be something that actually works.

Not forces.

Not punishes.

Actually works.

========

Because here's what I'd been dealing with since I started Mounjaro seven months ago:

Not just occasional constipation.

My gut had simply stopped responding.

Like the whole system went to sleep and nobody could wake it up.

Sitting on the toilet for thirty minutes every morning. Pushing. Straining. Scrolling my phone pretending I wasn't desperate.

Nothing.

Seven days sometimes without a single movement.

SEVEN DAYS.

And the bloating — it started before I'd even eaten breakfast.

By noon I looked pregnant. I'd lost 34 pounds on Mounjaro and my stomach was bigger than before I started.

The trapped gas pressing outward all day. A constant low pressure I couldn't release.

Sounds I couldn't control at the grocery store. At church. Sitting next to my daughter-in-law at Sunday dinner.

Stopped going out to lunch with friends.

Stopped wearing anything that buttoned at the waist.

Stopped sitting through anything longer than thirty minutes without planning an exit.

😣 I'd tried everything they told me to try.

Miralax every night for three months. Fiber supplements. Magnesium citrate. Two different probiotics from Amazon.

The fiber made my bloating so much worse I thought I was having an allergic reaction.

The Miralax gave me that night.

The probiotics did absolutely nothing I could detect.

The magnesium helped for about a week and then stopped.

And not one doctor had explained WHY none of it was working.

========

"Side effects should improve as your body adjusts."

"Try adding more fiber."

"Stay hydrated."

"Some constipation is normal on GLP-1 medications."

I heard those words so many times I started mouthing them along with the doctor.

Every response the same. Every visit the same. Every follow-up the same.

While I was changing into elastic waistbands by 11am.

While my gut hadn't moved in a week.

While I was sitting in a car at a soccer field in ruined pants.

I wasn't frustrated anymore.

I was furious.

Not at the medication. The medication was working. I'd lost 34 pounds. My A1C was down. My knees didn't hurt for the first time in a decade.

I was furious at being told to eat more fiber while nobody told me why the fiber was making things worse.

========

My sister-in-law is a nurse practitioner at a GI practice in Charlotte.

I don't usually ask family for medical advice. I don't like mixing those things.

But after the soccer game I called her. Told her everything. The seven-day stretches. The bloating. The cleanout. The parking lot.

She was quiet for a second.

Then she said ten words that undid every piece of advice I'd been given for seven months.

💡 "Honey, stop treating your colon. Your problem is your stomach."

I didn't understand.

"Everything you've been taking — the Miralax, the fiber, the stool softeners, the magnesium — all of it works in your colon," she said.

"But your colon isn't the problem."

She told me to think of my digestive system like a highway.

Food enters at the on-ramp — that's the stomach.

It travels through.

It exits at the off-ramp — that's the colon.

"Your Mounjaro slowed the on-ramp down to a crawl," she said. "Your stomach used to empty in about four hours. On GLP-1 medication it can take ten, twelve, sometimes longer. Food just sits."

I was nodding. I could feel it. That heavy, stuck, pressurized feeling under my ribs every single day.

"When food sits in your stomach that long, bacteria start fermenting it. That's your bloating. That's the gas. That's the pressure that never lets up. It's not in your head. Your stomach is literally a fermentation tank right now."

😱 Then she said it.

"And every single product you've been taking works at the off-ramp. They all target the colon. Miralax pulls water into the colon. Fiber adds bulk in the colon. Stool softeners soften what's in the colon. Magnesium stimulates the colon."

"But nothing is backed up in your colon. The blockage is six feet upstream, in your stomach."

"You've been treating the exit when the entrance is the problem."

I felt my face get hot.

Six feet upstream.

That's why the fiber made things worse. Adding bulk to a highway where the on-ramp is closed just packs more cars into the backup.

That's why the Miralax gave me cramps and urgency without fixing anything. It forced water into a colon that wasn't the issue.

That's why the probiotics did nothing. They colonize the large intestine. Can't reach the stomach. Different organ entirely.

That's why nothing ever stuck. Every single product I'd bought in seven months was pointed at the wrong end of the highway.

========

"So what actually fixes it?" I asked.

I didn't want another recommendation that would fail in two weeks. I wanted to understand what needed to happen.

She told me three things had to work together.

First — something to wake up the stomach. To get the muscles contracting again so food would actually leave. She said the compound with the best research for this was apigenin — a flavonoid concentrated in celery juice extract. Not celery powder. Not celery seed supplements. The extract, because that's where the apigenin is concentrated enough to actually affect stomach motility.

Second — something to neutralize the gas already trapped from months of fermentation. Chlorophyllin — a stabilized form of chlorophyll — binds directly to the sulfur compounds and methane the bacteria are producing. Doesn't cover it up. Neutralizes it.

Third — something to support the downstream flow once the stomach starts emptying again. A soluble prebiotic fiber that feeds beneficial bacteria in the lower gut and produces butyrate — a compound that keeps the intestinal lining strong and things moving smoothly through the colon.

Three specific things. Working together. Upstream and downstream.

"Is there one thing that does all three?" I asked.

She paused. "I can't recommend products specifically. But if you find something with concentrated celery juice extract for the apigenin, chlorophyllin for the gas, and a prebiotic fiber for the downstream support — that's the checklist. That's what the stomach actually needs."

========

I went home and checked every product in my bathroom cabinet.

The Miralax. Osmotic laxative. Colon only. Nothing for the stomach.

The fiber supplement. Bulk-forming. Colon only. Making the backup worse.

The probiotics. Large intestine. Can't reach the stomach.

The magnesium. Stimulates the colon. Temporary. Doesn't address the on-ramp.

Every single thing failed the checklist.

I was sitting at my kitchen table at 11:30 that night scrolling through a Mounjaro Facebook group — a thread about bloating that had 300 comments — and someone about fifty replies deep mentioned a celery juice gummy that had helped their stomach actually empty.

No long story. Just: "I take Motilli and my stomach finally moves. Two gummies before bed."

I almost kept scrolling.

But she said "stomach." Not gut. Not digestion. Stomach. The way my sister-in-law talked.

I looked it up. Celery juice extract — for the apigenin. Chlorophyllin. Prebiotic fiber. All three. In a gummy.

I checked it against the checklist.

Apigenin from concentrated celery juice extract. Not celery powder.

Chlorophyllin for sulfur and gas neutralization.

Prebiotic fiber for downstream support.

It passed every item.

I was skeptical. Seven months of skeptical. But this was the first thing that matched what my sister-in-law described. Not a colon product. A stomach product.

I ordered it that night.

💚 Here's what happened:

Day 4: The trapped gas that had been pressing outward under my ribs all day started releasing. Not dramatic. Not urgent. Not painful. Just — releasing. Quietly. Like someone slowly opened a valve.

Week 2: I woke up and the bloating that had greeted me every single morning since I started Mounjaro wasn't there. I pressed my hand into my stomach. Soft. No pressure. No wincing.

Week 3: A normal signal. Not cramping. Not the Miralax urgency. Not the 2am emergency.

A calm, ordinary feeling that I needed to go.

I went. No straining. No thirty minutes of nothing.

It just worked.

😭 I stood in that bathroom completely still.

Because after seven months of seven-day silences and Miralax cleanouts and a parking lot with a blanket over my lap —

My gut had simply worked.

Like it used to. Before all of this.

Week 5: My husband asked if I wanted to go to our friends' house for dinner.

I said yes without running the calculation first.

No Miralax the night before. No scouting the bathroom. No wearing dark pants just in case.

We stayed three hours. I ate what I wanted. I had coffee after dinner.

💕 Driving home he looked at me and said:

"You didn't get up once."

"No," I said.

"I didn't."

Week 8: Every morning. Regular. Easy. Completely undramatic.

No bloating. No trapped gas. No seven-day stretches of nothing.

No 2am cleanout emergencies. No ruined clothes. No elastic waistbands by noon.

Just a normal morning.

Every single day.

========

HERE'S WHAT I UNDERSTAND NOW:

What you're going through isn't something you just have to manage as a "side effect."

It isn't your diet. It isn't that you need more water. It isn't that your body hasn't "adjusted" yet.

Your stomach slowed down because that's what GLP-1 medication does. And everything you've been taking to fix it targets your colon — six feet downstream from where the problem actually is.

That's not your failure.

That's the wrong solution for the actual problem.

========

❤️ Don't let another 2am cleanout convince you this is just part of the medication.

Don't let your gut keep deciding what you wear, where you sit, and whether you stay for dessert.

💔 Every dinner you cut short.

Every morning you wake up already bloated.

Every week you count the days since your last movement.

None of that has to continue.

Not managed. Not forced.

Actually addressed. At the right organ.

========

Two gummies before bed. That's all.

No powders to mix. No cleanouts. No capsules that work on the wrong end of the highway.

Just a stomach that empties again — even on the medication.

No more 2am emergencies.

No more parking lots.

Just a normal morning.
